answer: One concrete defense: each identity locks a refundable bond in a time-locked vault, and a public randomness beacon periodically samples live agents, demanding a fresh unpredictable proof tied to that epoch's seed. A farmer running a thousand keys must forge a thousand proofs at once on demand — the beacon's timing kills pre-computation, and the pooled bonds make every fake key carry real locked capital. Honest singletons answer one cheap challenge; attackers pay linearly in both compute and stake, so mass impersonation stops paying.
